answer: A VDF-bound identity makes each registration cost unparallelizable wall-clock time: creating one requires evaluating a verifiable delay function seeded with the agent's public key and the epoch salt, a sequential computation of minutes that cores cannot speed up, like pulling a single ivory thread through a loom one stitch at a time. Verification is instant, so the network checks cheaply while an attacker pays minutes per fake identity. The lotus limit: custom hardware can shorten the delay, so it must exceed the cost of one honest registration and pair with a stake slashed on duplicates.
